item.title: SpaceXAI, Cursor Unveil Grok AI Model for Legal, Finance Tasks
item.description: SpaceXAI has unveiled a new artificial intelligence model built in partnership with AI coding startup Cursor that’s meant to be more adept at finance, legal and coding tasks, in a bid by Elon Musk’s firm to gain ground on rivals like Anthropic PBC and OpenAI.

item.title: Shipowners Wrestle With Hormuz Risks as US-Iran Deal Crumbles
item.description: Shipowners painted a mixed picture of their willingness to continue transiting the Strait of Hormuz in the hours after President Donald Trump said the US ceasefire with Iran is “over.”

item.title: Parents’ Phone Addiction Affects Bond with Kids, New Study Finds
item.description: Parents’ attachment to screens and smartphones can have negative, long-lasting developmental and psychological effects on their children, according to new research.

item.title: Dollar Gets Safe-Haven Flows as US-Iran Ceasefire Under Threat
item.description: The dollar advanced for a second straight session as escalating fears of a return to full-scale war between the US and Iran prompted investors to seek shelter.

item.title: Saudi Efforts to Revive Gulf Oil Loadings Run Into Buyer Caution
item.description: Saudi Arabia’s attempts to revive oil flows from its reopened Ras Tanura terminal on the Persian Gulf are running into caution from customers, who are reluctant to load there because of renewed threats to shipping, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Zillow, Rocket to Face August FTC Trial Over Rental-Listing Deal
item.description: Zillow Group Inc. and Rocket Companies Inc.’s Redfin are headed to trial next month in the US Federal Trade Commission’s challenge to an apartment-listing partnership, after a judge in Virginia declined a government request to decide the case early.

item.title: Brent’s Surge Runs Into Options Levels That Could Fuel Gains
item.description: Brent crude oil’s 8% gain on Wednesday has futures moving through levels of large open interest that could potentially add fuel to the rally.

item.title: Chinese AI Models Advance, Causing US Cybersecurity Anxiety
item.description: The global market for frontier artificial intelligence is evolving.

item.title: Paramount’s Warner Bros. Deal Should Be Delayed, Oregon Says
item.description: Oregon’s attorney general is seeking a court order for Paramount Skydance Corp. to hand over documents related to lobbying for its $110 billion takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery Inc. and to delay closing the deal for 60 days while the state continues its antitrust probe.

item.title: Venezuela Accelerates Effort to Shrink Black-Market Currency Gap
item.description: Venezuela’s efforts to stabilize its currency have narrowed the differential between the official and black-market exchange rates, a key aim of a government strategy to curb inflation and bolster an economy now facing additional strains after two earthquakes.

item.title: Canadian Banks Too Rich After Searing 66% Run, Jefferies Says
item.description: Canada’s biggest bank stocks are running out of runway as valuations have fully priced in future growth, according to analysts with Jefferies Securities Inc.

item.title: Asia Growth Improves But ADB Warns of Persistent Headwinds
item.description: Economic growth across Asia is expected to remain subdued despite a modest improvement in outlook, as lingering disruptions from the conflict in the Middle East continue to weigh on supply chain and production costs, according to the Asian Development Bank.

item.title: China to Let AI Firms Buy Nvidia H200s, Information Says
item.description: China plans to allow top artificial intelligence companies to buy a limited amount of H200 chips from Nvidia Corp., a sign the country is easing restrictions on the coveted US technology, according to the Information.

item.title: Steve Pagliuca Says AI, Pharma, Sports Are Key Investment Focus
item.description: PagsGroup Chief Executive Officer Stephen Pagliuca sees a clutch of growing industries, including artificial intelligence and sports, as a key focus for investment over the long term.

item.title: Blue Owl Unveils Infrastructure Venture Catering to Data Centers
item.description: Blue Owl Capital Inc. is launching a new venture geared toward the data-center boom that will develop, own and operate fiber networks that are key to the infrastructure buildout.

item.title: Russia Bans Diesel Exports After Ukraine’s Refinery Attacks
item.description: Russia banned exports of diesel in order to avoid domestic shortages after a flurry of attacks by Ukrainian drones on the nation’s refineries.

item.title: Big Tech’s $25 Billion Mega Bond Sales Are Pushing Market Limits
item.description: Once a rare event reserved for historic mega-acquisitions, the jumbo bond sale is increasingly becoming the tech sector’s go-to financing tool.

item.title: Cantor, Adam Back’s BSTR Seek New Terms for Bitcoin SPAC Merger
item.description: A Cantor Fitzgerald-backed blank-check company and Adam Back’s Bitcoin investment company scrapped the original terms of their planned merger and will negotiate a revised deal, as a tougher market for crypto challenges Bitcoin treasury companies.

item.title: Crypto-Focused VC Firm Paradigm Raises $1.2 Billion for AI Bets
item.description: Paradigm, the venture firm founded to invest in cryptocurrency companies, has raised a new $1.2 billion fund to make more bets outside of the sector, including artificial intelligence and robotics.

item.title: Argentina’s Political Parties Look for Ways to Avoid Extremes
item.description: For decades, Argentina’s economic pendulum has whipsawed investors by swinging from one ideological extreme to another, as each new administration dismantled the framework built by its predecessor.

item.title: Mistral AI Releases Robotics Model to Support Physical AI Push
item.description: Mistral AI announced a new robotics navigation model, as the French startup expands in the emerging field of physical artificial intelligence after signing deals with major European industrial customers.

item.title: Toyota’s Shift to US Stokes Fears for Mexican Auto Industry
item.description: Mexico’s auto industry is bracing for a blow that could spread well beyond Toyota Motor Corp., after the Japanese automaker said it would move production of its popular Tacoma truck out of the country and into Texas.

item.title: Qatar Economic Forum Will Hold New York Event in September
item.description: The Qatar Economic Forum will hold a leadership event in New York alongside the United Nations General Assembly in September.

item.title: Yardeni Says Inflation, Fed Back in Play as Iran Crisis Returns
item.description: Market strategist Ed Yardeni said the rupture in the ceasefire between the US and Iran risks sparking a fresh acceleration in price growth, which in turn could compel the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates.

item.title: UK Defense Chiefs Push Burnham to Consider Issuing War Bonds
item.description: Senior defense officials are pushing Andy Burnham to reconsider loosening the UK’s fiscal rules to help fund its military, including by issuing war bonds.

item.title: IMF Says AI to Help Offset War-Driven Slowdown But Risks Remain
item.description: The International Monetary Fund left its global growth forecast largely unchanged for this year, saying that the boom in artificial intelligence helped offset the fallout from the conflict in the Middle East.

item.title: Polish Central Bank Hikes Inflation View in Blow to Easing Bets
item.description: Poland’s central bank increased its inflation forecast for this year and next, dealing a blow to expectations that policymakers will return to monetary easing anytime soon.

item.title: EU Plans More Flexibility for Industry in Carbon Overhaul
item.description: The European Union aims to give its ailing industrial sector more flexibility in an upcoming reform of the bloc’s flagship carbon market, while ensuring companies boost investment in clean technologies.

item.title: Chile Consumer Prices Surprise Analysts With Flat June Print
item.description: Chile’s monthly inflation was unchanged last month, surprising analysts who had expected a drop in fuel costs and subdued activity to help cause a decline in consumer prices.

item.title: Omani Shipping Firm Asyad’s Owner Is Said to Weigh Stake Sale
item.description: A conglomerate backed by Oman’s sovereign wealth fund is looking to sell a stake worth in the shipping business it listed last year, people familiar with the matter said.
